title: The Fastest Cars In GTA 6 And How To Get Them
summary: The state of Leonida is home to some of the rarest and most expensive cars we've ever seen in the Grand Theft Auto franchise. GTA 6 features over a dozen supercars, which are always the pinnacle of the vehicle food chain. While you'll likely take any supercar during the early or mid-game, you'll eventually want to drive the fastest car in GTA 6. Driving the fastest car in Leonida will require you to acquire a legendary vehicle or wait until your character can afford one later on in the story. With GTA 6's new car-stealing restrictions , you can't just take a supercar off the streets and make it your own. However you decide to get a supercar, you'll still want to know which ones go the fastest. Fastest cars in GTA 6 Technically, the fastest overall cars in GTA 6 will depend on what custom mods you have installed on certain cars. For example, you can bring a car's max speed to 9.0 or higher (out of 10) by upgrading its engine, transmission, and more, but that's not the car's default speed. For this list, we'll just be covering which cars are the fastest by default in GTA 6. This means looking at the car's stock speed when it has no additional upgrades installed. This list is also just cars, as we'll go over the fastest overall vehicles, including motorcycles, planes, and bikes, in a future list. Here are the top five fastest cars we've come across in GTA 6, ranked by their top speeds: 5. Pfister Comet S2 Coming in as the fifth-fastest car in GTA 6 is the Pfister Comet S2, a slight surprise since this vehicle isn't classified as a supercar. However, it's plenty fast, with a stock speed rating of 7.7, beating out some truly impressive supercars that look like they would be faster. Without spoiling anything from the story, the Comet S2 is an option you could acquire later on in GTA 6. 4. Piccia Furia You knew some Italian muscle was going to be on this list, and the Piccia Furia comes in as the fourth-fastest car in GTA 6. Featuring a stock speed rating of 7.8, the Furia is a fairly rare car in Leonida, as you don't often see it parked at the luxurious NINE1NINE strip club or along the streets of the Vice City beaches. 3. Pegassi Vitello Pegassi has long been one of the best car brands in the GTA franchise, so it's no surprise to see it on this list. In GTA 6, the Pegassi Vitello is the third-fastest car in the game, with a stock speed rating of 8.2. There's a significant gap between the Vitello and the two slower cars on this list in terms of speed, acceleration, and handling. 2. Progen Emerus GTA Online players will immediately recognize the Progen Emerus, and it's made a return in GTA 6. When it's fully maxed out with upgrades and mods, the Emerus can reach a speed rating of 9.0 and above. However, even with all of its stock parts, you'll have a speed rating of 8.3 with the Progren Emerus. 1. Truffade Thrax Topping the list of the fastest cars in GTA 6 is the Truffade Thrax. This supercar is significantly faster than anything else we've found so far in Leonida, featuring a stock speed rating of 8.7. That's higher than most cars can reach with fully upgraded parts, so you're going to be flying with the Thrax if you can manage to fully upgrade it. To guarantee getting one, read our guide on the NoFlusher tag locations . For some honorable mentions, we have the Pegassi Tempesta (7.6 speed rating) and the Granforma Zorrusso (7.5 speed rating). New cars that haven't been discovered yet in GTA 6 could change this list in the future, but these are the fastest cars known to be in the game right now. For more on GTA 6, from completing side missions to finding a tricky location on the sprawling map of Leonida, we’ve got you covered with our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub .

title: GTA 6 Tenebrae Lux Walkthrough And All Puzzle Solutions
summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 offers non-stop action. You can spend numerous hours taking down rival gangsters, escaping from annoying cops, or just doing odd jobs to rake in a lot of dough. However, if you want something that’s more befuddling than usual, you can tackle intricate puzzles in a video game called Tenebrae Lux. We’ve got all the solutions for you in this guide. In This Article Tenebrae Lux and the JoySystem console Tenebrae Lux Sliding Block Puzzles Additional puzzles and collectible documents - Part 1 Tenebrae Lux Bunker Phone Puzzle Randomized dates Room anomalies What to do in succeeding rooms Numerical equivalents for each anomaly Zuchworks Engine Greek letter Telephone rings Painting of Roman-style pillars Tape recorder Classified document Photo Desk lamp and morse code Clock Vinyl record Music Bunker Phone Puzzle solution Additional collectible documents - Part 2 Tenebrae Lux Ruins and Bridge Puzzle The bridge and the symbols The poem and symbolic words Ruins and Bridge Puzzle solution Additional collectible documents - Part 3 Tenebrae Lux Lighthouse Doors Puzzle Tenebrae Lux and the JoySystem console Tenebrae Lux is a “video game within a video game.” You can play it once you have access to the JoySystem console , which occurs during a main mission called Feng Shui. In the GTA 6 Tenebrae Lux game, you play as someone simply known as “The Man.” You find yourself stranded on an island, and your goal is to solve puzzles to reach the lighthouse at the top of the hill. What makes the whole experience memorable is that the game is purely in black and white, and its atmosphere is further enhanced by eerie sound effects, disturbing visuals, and randomized clues/content. Tenebrae Lux Sliding Block Puzzles When you first start Tenebrae Lux, you’ll see the lighthouse in the distance. To your left, you’ll spot a fishing wharf and a couple of rundown shacks. At this point, you need to interact with the game boards in the area to do the Sliding Block Puzzles. There are two in the wharf and one in the small shack just beside it. Here’s what the Sliding Block Puzzle mechanics entail: There are three types of pieces on the board: pyramids, square plates, and stacked blocks. Your goal is to clear out/destroy everything. The pyramids can be moved horizontally or vertically until they hit the board edge or another object. They remain intact after destroying adjacent square plates, but they’re expended if they destroy a block. Stacked blocks can also be moved and they destroy adjacent pyramids. However, they have no effect on square plates. You mostly just move them to create a path so your pyramids don’t end up adjacent to them unless absolutely necessary. Square plates cannot be moved at all. A bit of trial and error is necessary, and you can reset by exiting the board interface. Likewise, the types of pieces and their placement on each board tends to be randomized per playthrough, so there’s no clear-cut solution for everything. Note 1: Once you’ve completed the three required Sliding Block Puzzles, you’re free to enter the bunker. Note 2: Don’t forget to pick up the document next to one of the puzzle boards in the wharf. There are 11 documents in total, and not everything can be discovered in a single playthrough. Additional puzzles and collectible documents - Part 1 You’ll realize that there are a some some strange occurrences in your surroundings: The haunted shack atop the sloping path has its front door locked. However, if you check the porch at the back, you’ll see an optional Sliding Block Puzzle. Solve it to enter the shack so you can pick up a document. If you follow the coastal path, you’ll stumble upon a mysterious door at the edge of a pier. It’s the “Door That Leads to Nowhere.” Just beyond that, there’s another optional Sliding Block Puzzle. It unlocks the cargo container, which has one more document. Tenebrae Lux Bunker Phone Puzzle Once you’re ready, go through the well-lit door opposite the wharf. It leads you to the GTA 6 Tenebrae Lux Bunker Phone Puzzle, which is, in our opinion, one helluva doozy. Upon entering the main room in the bunker, you’ll see all sorts of gizmos and contraptions. Now, you have to keep your eyes peeled for clues related to anomalies. Note: We encourage you to enable subtitles and closed captions so you don’t miss out on voiceover hints. Randomized dates Each time you enter the bunker room, that particular instance can be one of six potential dates: October 11, October 14, October 20, October 23, October 27, or October 30. You can find out what day it is by inspecting the calendar on the wall. Your character will either make an off-handed remark about it or you’ll see dates that have been crossed out. It’s important that you know what day it is for that particular instance since you need to figure out a specific anomaly. This mechanic is also tied to the solution for the puzzle. Room anomalies There are several objects that you need to check in the room. We’ve listed them based on how early you’ll see or hear them upon entering: Zuchworks Engine Greek letter - The moment you enter the room, you might see this notification: “Developed using Zuchworks Engine.” This might have a Greek alphabet--i.e. alpha, beta, gamma, and so on. Telephone rings - Upon entering the room, the phone might ring. Count how many times it rings. Music - Upon entering the room, you’ll hear music (like an old-timey shanty of sorts). Listen closely to the speed of the music and any distortion. Painting of Roman-style pillars - On the shelf to your right. Look at the pillars to see if they form a Roman numeral. Tape recorder - On the desk to your right. See if it can be played and listen to the date. Classified document - On the desk to your right. Check if the Cascade File Number is written down or redacted. Photo - On the desk to your right. Count how many people are in the photograph. Vinyl record - On the metal barrels at the left-hand side of the room. Check the price of The Bateson Brothers record. Desk lamp and morse code - The lamp that you need to check is to the left of the calendar. A document about morse code might appear on the console terminal. Clock - Above the console terminal. Look at the time. Note: Keep in mind that not all of these objects will appear in your playthrough. For instance, you might not see a painting on the shelf or you might not be able to interact with the document or tape recorder. That’s totally fine. There will always be six important objects among the options listed above. What to do in succeeding rooms Okay, you’ve checked the date on the calendar and you’ve also inspected the six objects in the initial room. Don’t forget to take a screenshot of each of them or jot down the details in your Notes app. Then, go through the door to the right of the phone and head up the steps. Surprise! You’re back in the same room… but there’s something fishy going on. Go ahead and investigate the calendar to learn about the current date for that particular instance--i.e. the second room. Then, inspect the six objects in the room once more. Be on the lookout for any changes that are out of the ordinary. Examples include the clock showing a different time, the vinyl record having a different price, or the desk lamp suddenly flickering on and off. Whatever seems oddly different is the anomaly for that date. Jot down these details and go up the steps again. You’ll be in the same room, but the calendar date, as well as the anomaly, should be different. Keep doing this until you’ve investigated six instanced bunker rooms. Numerical equivalents for each anomaly Let’s say you’ve already listed the anomalies for each instance/calendar date. Now, it’s time to figure out their numerical equivalents. Zuchworks Engine Greek letter If all six rooms had the Zuchworks Engine notification, then the one with a different Greek letter is the anomaly. Each Greek letter corresponds to a number: Alpha = 1 Beta = 2 Gamma = 3 Delta = 4 Epsilon = 5 Digamma = 6 Zeta = 7 Eta = 8 Theta = 9 Telephone rings If the telephone rings in all six rooms, then the one with a different number of rings is the anomaly. That’s the numerical value that you should list down. Painting of Roman-style pillars The pillars form Roman numerals--i.e. “III” is 3, “VIII” is 8, “XIII” is 13, and so on. Whatever is different from others is the anomaly. Note that if you get a double-digit result, you must add the two digits. So 12 becomes “1+2 = 3,” and 13 becomes “1+3 = 4.” You get the idea. Tape recorder You’ll hear The Man (yourself) mention the date, and the odd one out is the anomaly. You need to check which number is different from others. Here’s an example: Let’s say the date mentioned in most rooms is October 11, 1926. The anomaly is October 1 9 , 1926. Then the answer is “9” since that’s the altered number. If the anomaly is something like October 20 , 1926, then you have to add “2+0 = 2.” That’s because a couple of numbers got changed. Classified document Read the header of the document and check the protocol number if it’s not redacted. Then, get the sum of the two digits. Photo Count the number of people in the photo--i.e. the one that’s different from the others in instanced rooms. Desk lamp and morse code This one is a bit trickier. If the desk lamp flashes, you need to check the document with the morse code. Examples: One quick flicker, followed by four longer flashes = 1. Five quick flickers = 5. Three long flashes, followed by two quick flickers = 8. Five long flashes = 0. As usual, whatever is the odd one out is the anomaly. So, just write down the numerical equivalent. Clock If the time on the clock is in play, you should see a book that says: “The Angle of the Hour… from hour to minute.” This means you have to look at the angle created by the gap between the hour hand and the minute hand. Example: 3:00 - The angle is 90 degrees or 9+0 = 9. 7:00 - The angle is 150 degrees or 1+5 = 6. Vinyl record The price of The Bateson Brothers record might be different. Add the two numbers and get the sum. Music If the music plays and gets distorted in one of the rooms, you can refer to the clues on the vinyl records. You’ll notice that The Bateson Brothers album is played at 45 rpm, whereas the Nyles Connor album is played at 33 rpm. The slowed down/distorted anomaly is 33 rpm or “3+3 = 6.” Bunker Phone Puzzle solution The solution to the GTA 6 Tenebrae Lux Bunker Phone Puzzle is based on the anomalies in each date arranged chronologically--i.e. October 11, 14, 20, 23, 27, and, lastly, 30. That’s why it’s imperative that you check the calendar in every instanced room that you enter. We’ve got an example for you from our playthrough, but do know that the solution tends to be different per player/each run: October 11 anomaly: Tape recorder This was October 20, 1926; everything else was October 11, 1926. 2+0 = 2. October 14 anomaly: Clock The time was 7:00. The time in all other rooms was at 3:00. 150 degrees is 1+5 = 6. October 20 anomaly: Classified document The non-redacted protocol file number was 42. 4+2 = 6. October 23 anomaly: Phone This rang twice, though it rang thrice in the other rooms. Three rings = 3. October 27 anomaly: Music The music was slowed down and distorted (33 rpm). 3+3 = 6 October 30 anomaly: Zuchworks Engine This one had gamma while everything else had beta. Once you have all six numbers, key those in, followed by the pound/hash sign. Given the example from our playthrough, the solution we got was: 2-6-6-2-6-3-#. Additional collectible documents - Part 2 After solving the Bunker Phone Puzzle, don’t forget to grab a couple of collectibles: See if the room next to the barrels/vinyl records can be opened. Inside, you’ll find an emaciated creature that’s holding a diagram. Then, once you exit, some of the shelves in the main room should topple over, revealing a collectible document. Continue up the cliffside path. At the halfway point by the railings, you’ll see another document. Tenebrae Lux Ruins and Bridge Puzzle The Tenebrae Lux Ruins and Bridge Puzzle in GTA 6 is also another brain-bursting activity. Here’s a quick summary: Right in front of you, you should see ruined structures surrounded by objects on pedestals. These objects include: Sundial Moon statue Tree Brazier Trophy Earthen pot Fountain There are glowing runes/strange symbols etched into sections of the ruins. There’s a poem in a memorial to your left. Note: If you go to the back section of the ruins, you might find a collectible document on top of a wooden crate. The bridge and the symbols Head up the sloping path to stumble upon a bridge… which happens to have the same runic symbols that are glowing. Your goal in the Lux Ruins and Bridge Puzzle is to (a) read the poem and look for keywords or themes, (b) check for the corresponding objects/sculptures, and (c) find the runic symbol that aligns with that object. You have to step on seven symbols to cross the bridge. It’s a bit like Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade, wouldn’t you say? Note 1: You’re allowed to make two mistakes in the first six segments of the bridge. If you make a third mistake, or if you fail on the last segment, you’ll fail. Note 2: Failure causes everything to reset and get randomized. The placements of the objects and runes will be different. Heck, even the lines on the poem will be different, too. The poem and symbolic words The poem is called “The Eternal March,” so feel free to ignore that title. Instead, you have to look at the remaining seven lines. Read the poem carefully so you can ascertain symbolic and thematic words as they relate to the objects around the ruins: Sundial = Sun, solar, sunrise. Moon statue = Moon, lunar, evening, night, sleep. Tree = Forest, woods. Brazier = Fire, flames, fiery. Trophy = Gold, trove, treasure, prize. Earthen pot = Ground, soil, earth, mound. Fountain = Water, wetlands, swamps, drinking. Note 1: In some cases, a single line on the poem might evoke two object themes--i.e. “Through shadowed forests, then mines of gold.” This means you need to step on the runic symbol that matches the tree, followed by the trophy. Note 2: You can’t step on the same runic symbol on the bridge. For example: If the poem mentions “fire” or “flames” a few times, you only need to step on the brazier's matching symbol once. Ignore the other instances that similar words appear in the poem. Ruins and Bridge Puzzle solution The poem and solution to the GTA 6 Ruins and Bridge Puzzle in Tenebrae Lux is based on our playthrough, so things will be vastly different for your run. Important: When glancing at runic symbols, you should position yourself so that the runic symbol is in front of you and nearby, and you have a full view of the object that it’s supposed to match. You can see these in the succeeding images. Line 1: “Walking as one through forests vast and deep” = Tree. Line 2: “ Troves of shining riches adorn our path” = Trophy. Line 3: “ Furrowed ground lies heavy beneath our marching feet” = Earthen pot. Line 4: “ Sleeping soundly under the burning heat ” = Moon and brazier. Line 5: “Striding onward beneath the lunar glow” = We ignored this one since we already stepped on the moon’s matching symbol. Line 6: “Marching through the flames then wetlands vast” = We ignored the mention of "flames" since we already used the brazier's matching symbol earlier. So we moved on to the next object, which was the fountain. Line 7: “Then resting ‘til finally the sunrise calls us forth” = Sun. Additional collectible documents - Part 3 After crossing the bridge, take a look at the small building to the right. If it's not locked, you can enter it and grab the collectible document. Tenebrae Lux Lighthouse Doors Puzzle The Lighthouse Doors Puzzle in Tenebrae Lux is, thankfully, a lot easier than the riddles in previous areas. Initially, you’ll see a “Slenderman” figure walking toward one of seven doors. (To be frank, it does remind us more of the creepy fella from Exit 8.) The goal here is fairly simple: You just need to go through the door that’s the farthest away from the Slenderman-esque NPC. If the NPC uses the first/leftmost door, then you should pass through the seventh/rightmost door. If the NPC uses the sixth door, then you should pass through the first door. Later, you’ll see two and even three NPCs walking toward doorways. To complicate matters, some doors might even be out of order. The same concept still applies: Among all the available doors, you have to pick the one that’s farthest away from all existing NPCs. Let’s say NPC #1 used the first door, the second and third doors are unavailable, NPC #2 used the fourth door, and NPC #3 used the seventh door. You must pick the sixth door. Even though it’s adjacent to the third NPC, it’s still far enough from the first and second dudes. Anyway, this should help you finish this segment of the game. Congratulations! You’ve just solved the Tenebrae Lux puzzles in GTA 6. That being said, there are still plenty of secrets to discover, including some collectible documents that remain hidden. You’re going to feel lost as you explore the cities, beachfronts, and seedy underbelly of Leonida. If you need more help navigating the massive game world and tackling its activities, be sure to check our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub .
